title: Behaviour of Ideal Gas
short_intro: An ideal gas is a theoretical gas composed of a set of randomly moving point particles that interact only through elastic collisions. It strictly obeys the universal gas equation under all conditions of temperature and pressure.

exam_scope.tgt_core: Boyle's Law, Charles's Law, Gay-Lussac's Law, ideal gas equation PV = nRT, universal gas constant, and basic absolute temperature scale.
exam_scope.pgt_extension: Kinetic interpretation of temperature, Maxwell-Boltzmann velocity distribution, Van der Waals real gas corrections, and compressibility factor.

concept_notes.heading: Postulates of Kinetic Theory of Gases
bullets: All gases consist of a very large number of identical, rigid, spherical molecules moving in random directions with all possible speeds.
The actual volume occupied by the gas molecules is negligible compared to the total volume of the container.
Collisions between molecules and with the container walls are perfectly elastic, conserving both total momentum and kinetic energy.

concept_notes.heading: Equation of State for an Ideal Gas
bullets: The macroscopic behavior of an ideal gas is summarized by the equation PV = nRT, where n is the number of moles.
Alternatively, in terms of Boltzmann's constant, PV = NkT, where N is the total number of molecules and k = R/N_A.
The constant R has a value of approximately 8.314 J mol<sup>-1</sup> K<sup>-1</sup>.

concept_notes.heading: Kinetic Interpretation of Pressure
bullets: Pressure arises due to the continuous bombardment of gas molecules against the walls of the container.
The pressure exerted by an ideal gas is given by P = (1/3)mnv<sup>2</sup>_{rms}, where m is molecular mass, n is number density, and v_{rms} is root mean square velocity.
Pressure depends directly on the translational kinetic energy per unit volume of the gas.

concept_notes.heading: Absolute Temperature and Kinetic Energy
bullets: Temperature is a direct measure of the average translational kinetic energy of gas molecules.
For a monoatomic gas, the average kinetic energy per molecule is given by E = (3/2)kT.
At absolute zero (T = 0 K), the average kinetic energy of gas molecules theoretically drops to zero.

derivations.title: Pressure Exerted by an Ideal Gas
derivations.conditions: N identical molecules in a cubical container of side L
steps: Consider a molecule of mass m moving with velocity component v_x along the x-axis inside a cube of volume L<sup>3</sup>.
The change in momentum when the molecule undergoes an elastic collision with the wall perpendicular to the x-axis is Delta p_x = 2mv_x.
The time interval between successive collisions with the same wall is Delta t = 2L / v_x.
The force exerted by a single molecule on the wall is F_x = Delta p_x / Delta t = mv_x<sup>2</sup> / L.
Summing over all N molecules and taking the isotropic average v_x<sup>2</sup> = (1/3)v<sup>2</sup>_{rms}, the total pressure is P = F / L<sup>2</sup> = (1/3) (Nm/V) v<sup>2</sup>_{rms}.

derivations.title: Relation between Pressure and Kinetic Energy
derivations.conditions: Ideal gas containing N molecules in volume V
steps: Start from the kinetic theory expression for pressure: P = (1/3) (Nm/V) v<sup>2</sup>_{rms}.
Multiply and divide the right-hand side by 2 to introduce kinetic energy: P = (2/3) \times (1/2) (Nm v<sup>2</sup>_{rms}) / V.
Recognize that the total translational kinetic energy of the gas is E = (1/2) Nm v<sup>2</sup>_{rms}.
Substitute E into the pressure equation to obtain P = (2/3) (E / V).

graphs_and_experiments.title: Isotherms of an Ideal Gas (P vs V)
graphs_and_experiments.what_to_draw: A family of rectangular hyperbolas (curves sloping downward from left to right) for different constant temperatures T_3 > T_2 > T_1.
graphs_and_experiments.interpretation: Shows inverse proportionality between pressure and volume at constant temperature according to Boyle's law.
graphs_and_experiments.exam_use: Direct identification of isothermal curves and comparison of temperatures from P-V diagrams.

graphs_and_experiments.title: Isobars on P-T Diagram
graphs_and_experiments.what_to_draw: Straight lines passing through the origin (or extrapolating to -273.15 °C on Celsius scale) with different slopes for different pressures.
graphs_and_experiments.interpretation: Illustrates Charles's law where volume is directly proportional to absolute temperature.
graphs_and_experiments.exam_use: Finding slopes representing V/R ratios and determining absolute zero temperature.

graphs_and_experiments.title: Maxwell-Boltzmann Speed Distribution Curve
graphs_and_experiments.what_to_draw: Asymmetric bell-shaped curve plotting fraction of molecules against molecular speed, showing distinct peaks for most probable, average, and rms speeds.
graphs_and_experiments.interpretation: Demonstrates statistical distribution of molecular speeds at a given temperature.
graphs_and_experiments.exam_use: Relating peak position to temperature and distinguishing v_{mp}, v_{avg}, and v_{rms}.

solved_numericals.question: Find the root mean square velocity of oxygen molecules at 27 °C. Given R = 8.314 J mol<sup>-1</sup> K<sup>-1</sup> and molar mass of oxygen M = 32 × 10<sup>-3</sup> kg mol<sup>-1</sup>.
solution_steps: Convert temperature to Kelvin: T = 27 + 273 = 300 K.
Calculate the value: v_{rms} = \sqrt{74826 / 0.032} = \sqrt{2338312.5} \approx 483.5 \text{ m s<sup>-1</sup>}.

solved_numericals.question: Calculate the total translational kinetic energy of 2 moles of an ideal gas at 300 K. Take R = 8.314 J mol<sup>-1</sup> K<sup>-1</sup>.
solution_steps: Recall the formula for total internal kinetic energy of n moles of an ideal gas: E = (3/2) nRT.
Substitute the given values: n = 2, R = 8.314, T = 300.

solved_numericals.question: A given mass of an ideal gas occupies 400 mL at 27 °C and 700 mm Hg pressure. What will be its volume at standard temperature and pressure (0 °C and 760 mm Hg)?
solution_steps: Identify initial states: P_1 = 700 mm Hg, V_1 = 400 mL, T_1 = 27 + 273 = 300 K.
Identify final states: P_2 = 760 mm Hg, T_2 = 0 + 273 = 273 K, V_2 = ?.
Use combined gas law: (P_1 V_1) / T_1 = (P_2 V_2) / T_2.
Rearrange for V_2: V_2 = (P_1 V_1 T_2) / (P_2 T_1) = (700 \times 400 \times 273) / (760 \times 300).

assumptions_and_limitations: Assumption: Intermolecular forces are completely zero except during instantaneous elastic collisions. Limitation: Fails at high pressures where molecular volume and attractive forces become significant.

Assumption: Size of molecules is infinitesimally small compared to interparticle distance. Limitation: Fails at low temperatures near liquefaction point where real gases deviate heavily from ideal behavior.

common_misconceptions.wrong: Temperature is a measure of the total kinetic energy of all molecules in a body.
common_misconceptions.correct: Temperature is a measure of the average kinetic energy per molecule, not the total sum.
common_misconceptions.why: A large pool of water at low temperature has more total kinetic energy than a boiling drop of water, yet its temperature is lower.

common_misconceptions.wrong: Ideal gas molecules lose energy during wall collisions.
common_misconceptions.correct: Collisions with container walls are perfectly elastic.
common_misconceptions.why: By definition, kinetic energy is conserved in ideal gas collisions; otherwise, gas pressure would continuously decay over time.

quick_revision: PV = nRT governs macroscopic ideal gas behavior, where R is the universal gas constant.
Molecular Ideal Gas Equation: PV = NkT
